prevalence_guidance.primary_denominator: Distinct scientific families with at least one evidenced model-backed attempt. Exclude scripted-only and unrun families from a model-completion rate.
prevalence_guidance.classification: For each family separately code observed execution/completion failure, observed model refusal, valid adverse scientific outcome, and unknown due to coverage. Do not collapse these into one failure category.
prevalence_guidance.reporting: Report k/D families with at least one observed event and coverage per family; this is event presence, not per-call incidence. Multiple versions and retries remain one family. Give uncertain coverage explicitly; if u model-executed families cannot be assessed, show confirmed k/D and possible (k+u)/D instead of treating unknown as zero.
prevalence_guidance.bias: A family with many attempts has more chances to reveal at least one failure. This descriptive family prevalence is neither an unbiased failure-probability estimate nor an LLM capability benchmark.
prevalence_guidance.within_family_rates: Use only frozen homogeneous attempt/cohort manifests with complete denominator and assignment-level records; valid scientific losses remain outcomes, retries are not fresh independent samples. Terminal hub jobs are never a substitute for episode or request counts.
prevalence_guidance.scope_result: No scoped completed family in other.json is model-backed. Therefore these records contribute zero to a model-failure prevalence denominator, while their scripted scientific failures must still be reported.
